dataset.name: Wikispeedia navigation paths and link graph (Stanford SNAP), 4,604 articles
dataset.license: SNAP research dataset; cite West & Leskovec (WWW 2012) and West, Pineau & Precup (IJCAI 2009). Article content is Wikipedia, CC BY-SA.

protocol.pairSource: seeded stratified sample of the lab test pairs (data/pairs.json "test", 150 per difficulty): 20 per difficulty with seed 20261122, then 10 more per difficulty from the remainder with seed 20261123 (extension added after the first 60 because budget allowed; protocol unchanged)
protocol.difficulty: shortest path length: easy <= 2, medium 3, hard 4+ (same as the lab benchmark)
protocol.temperature: 0 where the provider allows it, provider default otherwise
protocol.temperatureNote: temperature 0 sent where the API accepts it; models whose settings show temperature null do not accept it (Claude 5.5 via current SDK, OpenAI reasoning models)
protocol.invalidMove: re-ask once, then the game fails
protocol.state: stateless per step: target, current page, path so far, full outgoing link list (no 50-link cap, no distance-based filtering)

priorWork.name: LLM-WikiRace (Ziomek et al., arXiv 2602.16902, 2026)
priorWork.note: 549k-page Wikipedia graph, models see link titles only, 30-step cap, up to 50 links per page pre-filtered by distance to target; best model wins about 29% of hard games (paths of 7-8); looping is the main failure. Code: github.com/JuliuszZiomek/LLM-WikiRace-Benchmark

priorWork.name: WikiRacing Language Models (Hugging Face Space, HuggingFaceTB/wikiracing-llms)
priorWork.note: play against open models on Wikipedia links, plus a parallel evaluation harness for running many model agents

priorWork.name: Margiotta, Croce and Basili, Evaluating Large Language Models on Wikipedia Graph Navigation: Insights from the WikiGame (CLiC-it 2025, CEUR-WS Vol-4112)
priorWork.note: about 4,000 human WikiGame start-goal sessions used to test whether LLMs navigate the link graph beyond memorized facts

references.scope: reference on full set: 450 test pairs (easy 150, medium 150, hard 150); our 90 LLM pairs are a seeded stratified subset of those same pairs. Per-pair reference results are not saved, so these numbers are NOT recomputed on the subset.
references.note: classical strategies and the trained model are search procedures with a page budget (pages opened, with backtracking); LLMs here walk one click at a time with no backtracking and 15 clicks max. costPerGameUsd for these is 0 API dollars: they run locally in the browser.

strategies.name: my model (base + human clicks), both ends

testMetric.name: next-click accuracy on unseen targets (top-scored link is on a shortest path)
